newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- AVIS EUROPE ON ROAD TO STOCK MARKET LISTING

Avis Europe, the largest car hire company on the continent, is to be floated on the stock market with an expected value of 700 million stg. The share offer will come over a decade since the company was floated in London and eight years after it was taken into private ownership again. Shareholders spent a year considering different options for the company, including a merger with the American Avis company, which floated Avis Europe on the London stock market in 1989 but which now owns just 8.7 per cent of it. The bid, which was revived last year, was an attempt to re-unite the two companies but it ran into tax problems.
-- HSBC TO TAKE OVER EVERSHOLT FOR ONE BILLION STG

This week could see the completion of the one billion stg takeover of Eversholt, the train leasing company, by banking group HSBC Holdings. HSBC's leading subsidiary, Forward Trust, has been in negotiations to buy Eversholt for nearly three months. The one billion stg sale would eclipse the sum paid for Porterbrook, the rival train leasing group bought by Stagecoach for 825 million stg. Forward Trust was the only name to be linked seriously with Eversholt since a sale was first suggested
last autumn.
-- WELCOME BREAK SALE IMMINENT

Granada is near to finding a buyer for its Welcome Break motorway service centres when final bids are submitted for the business. Welcome Break was acquired by Granada as part of its 3.9 billion stg takeover of Forte FTE.L. However, the deal gave the company a near monopoly of Britain's motorway services and Granada agreed with the Office of Fair Trading to sell the business by April. There are six major bidders for the group, including National Express, Michael Guthrie, the former Pizzaland entrepreneur, and venture capitalists believed to include Cinven.
THE TIMES
-- MAXWELL'S CAUTIOUS 'YES' TO HELP IN SEARCH FOR MISSING FUNDS

Mirror Group pensions funds have requested Kevin Maxwell to help them to recover up to 50 million stg of the funds' assets which are believed to be still missing. The funds' trustees, lead by chairman Phillip Sheriden, have asked Maxwell whether he would be free to help them to look for missing assets. Lawyers acting for Maxwell have advised him that answering questions about the missing pension fund assets could prejudice his defence to charges of fraud brought by the Serious Fraud Office. Maxwell now says that if he can help he will.
-- POLITICAL BIAS QUESTION OVER TUC STRATEGY

The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is set to launch a campaign to urge its eight million members to vote for the political party which offers them most rights at work. This has provoked the Conservative Party into accusing it of failing to do maintain the appearance of political neutrality. Friday will see TUC leaders launching a one million stg pre-election campaign focusing on employment rights, including the European social chapter and a minimum wage, one of the major issues dividing the main political parties.
-- G7 MINISTERS URGE MARKETS TO CURTAIL RUNAWAY DOLLAR

The Group of Seven finance ministers have told foreign exchange markets that they want to see a halt to the dollar's rise against other main currencies. Finance ministers were not clear about what price, if any, they are prepared to pay and there are worries that markets will be tempted to call their bluff. They agreed on the desirability of exchange rate stability at around current levels but left open the possibility of central banks intervening together if markets fail to heed their wishes.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REUTERS FISHES IN FT'S WATERS

Financial information group Reuters is planning a specialist financial newspaper, possibly called Reuters News, targeted at the City and in direct competition to the Financial Times. The company has appointed pollsters Mori to canvass opinions in the City on what the new paper should be like. Reuters will print on pink paper, similar to the FT, but will not necessarily publish in broadsheet format. The paper will carry comprehensive sports coverage as a means of distancing itself from its rival.
-- U.S. GROUP CHANGES STRATEGY IN EFFORT TO BREAK POWER DUOPOLY

Southern Electric International, the U.S. owner of South Western Electricity SWN.L, is planning to build a generating plant or contract a company to supply it with power after being thwarted in its merger with National Power. Chief financial officer Raymond Hill said that the company was attempting to determine which is more economical. Analysts say that Southern Electric wants to recreate the monopoly structure it enjoyed in America until it ran into a British veto of its move to link up with National Power. The Monopolies and Mergers Commission's decision to block the deal was only a minor setback as Sweb has paid off well.
-- LEAK HALTS PROPOSED CO-OP DEAL

A Stock Exchange leak inquiry is set to halt plans at Lanica Trust, one of the City's fastest-growing investment companies, to buy out profitable parts of the co-operative movement. The group confirmed it was to put proposals to the Co-operative Wholesale and Retail Societies to buy certain businesses spanning funeral parlours, garages, department stores, chemists and opticians. The deal would be worth 500 million stg and is only a part of a more ambitious expansion plan. However, James Capel, the broking advisers, are to ask for a Stock Exchange inquiry into how details of the deal leaked from institutional investors into the press.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- INDEPENDENT SUPPLIERS TO OPPOSE BRITISH GAS PRICE CUTS

Independent gas suppliers have said they would oppose plans by British Gas to make selective price cuts to homes in the southwest, in an attempt to gain a foothold in the emerging domestic market. British Gas claims competition in the region is well established, but the proposals, which are expected to be put to Ofgas are likely to anger the Gas Consumers' Council. The watchdog is concerned that poorer households have gained little from competition and have warned that those on low income or benefit were paying more for gas.
-- ABBEY TO RAISE SCOTAM STAKES

Abbey National is attempting to top Prudential's bid for Scottish Amicable of 1.9 billion stg. The banking and insurance group may make its original bid of 1.4 billion stg look more attractive to policyholders. However, insiders played down a report that a new offer could be as high as 2.2 billion stg. Abbey is offering 400 million stg for the goodwill of ScotAm, a sum which will be passed to policyholders, and one billion stg for the "embedded value" in the life fund.
-- LLOYDS TO PAY TWICE INFLATION RATE

Lloyds-TSB will set down a marker for the rest of the finance sector by offering its 60,000 staff a pay rise of around twice the rate of inflation. The offer of five per cent will affect wage negotiations elsewhere in industry at a time when most settlements are being struck at around three per cent. The deal could be an attempt to pave the way for the integration of the pay systems of the old Lloyds and TSB banks and to avoid the threat of industrial action.
